summary: OpenAI cut API and subscription-usage prices for GPT-5.6 Luna (80% less) and Terra (20% less), introduced a paid Fast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol replacing Priority Processing, and described efficiency work (kernel optimization, token-generation improvements) behind the price cuts.

mechanisms.reason: The lab states concrete serving-cost and token-generation efficiency gains achieved through kernel rewrites and experiments, not just a price cut.
mechanisms.quote: The kernel work helped reduce the end-to-end cost of serving the model by 20%, while its experiments increased token-generation efficiency by more than 15%.

mechanisms.reason: Lower prices are framed as making high-volume workloads economical at much greater scale, implying more tokens served in aggregate.
mechanisms.quote: At the lower-cost end, the new Luna and Terra prices make high-volume work economical at much greater scale.

practices.reason: Engineers building on these models get a stated, immediate change in cost and speed for the same models with no code change required.
practices.quote: Starting today, GPT‑5.6 Luna, our fastest and most affordable model, will cost 80% less, while GPT‑5.6 Terra, our balanced model for everyday work, will cost 20% less.

practices.reason: The kernel and token-generation efficiency gains are achieved by OpenAI's own model working on its own production infrastructure, not a technique exposed for external teams to apply.
practices.quote: Within a human-led process, Sol autonomously rewrote and optimized production kernels, designed and ran hundreds of experiments to improve token generation, and monitored training, intervening when problems arose.

practices.reason: Fast mode replaces the existing Priority Processing offering and changes API pricing/quota consumption, requiring teams to review budgets and tagging even though it is largely backward compatible.
practices.quote: We’re also introducing Fast mode in the API, which replaces our Priority Processing offering.

practices.reason: A named benchmark comparison is cited to support the cost-performance claim but is the lab's own evaluation and not handed over as a transferable instrument.
practices.quote: On professional work, as measured by Agents’ Last Exam, Luna outperforms Fable 5 at an estimated cost per task nearly 99% lower.

notable_reason: Concrete, quantified figures on autonomous model-driven kernel optimization (20% serving cost reduction, 15% token-generation efficiency gain) alongside an 80% price cut mark a real data point on the inference cost curve.
